success_patterns: The agent answered with the bare entity that the passages repeatedly tie to the clue's distinctive details (Thomas Hardy, Watts, history, Conch). It ignored noisy or off-topic passages.

When the clue only gave a generic descriptor of a named event or deal ('1853 purchase'), the agent answered with the full standard name including the generic head word ('Gadsden Purchase'). It did not strip the word.
For 'this film series', the agent gave the series name ('Scream'), not the specific installment the passages mostly discuss ('Scream 3').
For 'a predicate & one of these', the agent found the passages listing the full set of required parts and answered with the missing sibling ('subject'), not a word already in the clue.

The agent ignored jokes and filler in the clue ('If I eat it, can I hear the ocean?', 'Call up Clio...'). It used a local-term gloss ('locally referred to as lambi') to map to the common English name (conch).

patch.reasoning: Every success here came from reading the clue's factual core, matching it to the entity the passages repeat, and giving that entity at the right granularity and in its standard name form. The skill does not yet say three things. First, a generic head noun in the clue ('purchase') is kept when it is part of the standard name. Second, series or franchise clues want the series name, not an installment. Third, jokes and filler in the clue are decoration, and local or foreign terms should be answered with the common English name. It also does not cover 'X & one of these' clues, which want the missing sibling in a set. These edits are small, specific and do not conflict with the existing rules.

edits.target: do not append that role word to the answer.
edits.content: - Exception for named events, deals, treaties, wars and laws: when the clue gives only a generic descriptor with the head noun and no distinctive name ('1853 purchase that brought the U.S. to its present area', 'the 1945 conference', 'this 1930s program'), the answer is the distinctive name PLUS the standard head word ('Gadsden Purchase', not 'Gadsden'). The 'do not repeat clue words' rule is for a separate modifier already in the clue ('hasty' + pudding). Test: would an answer key list the entity with that head word? If yes, keep it.

edits.target: Other named entities in the clue are anchors, never the answer.
edits.content: - Match granularity. 'This film series / franchise / saga / show' wants the series name ('Scream'), not the particular installment the passages mostly discuss ('Scream 3') or its song. 'This subject in school' wants the general subject ('history'), not a sub-topic.

edits.target: The context passages about the topic usually reveal the link.
edits.content: - Jokes, asides and filler in the clue ('(If I eat it, can I hear the ocean?)', 'Need help in this subject? Call up...') are decoration. Answer from the factual core plus the anchor term. When the clue uses a local or foreign word ('In Haiti, lambi is this big spiral-shelled sea snail'), look for the passage that glosses it ('locally referred to as lambi') and answer with the common English name (Conch).

edits.target: asks for the title or category noun itself (Dalai Lama), not the individual named in the clue.
edits.content: - 'X needs A & one of these' / 'A, B and one of these': the clue already gives some members of a set. Find the passage listing the full set ('a subject and a predicate') and answer with the missing member ('subject'), never one already named in the clue.
